newsitem.title: USA: Spring-like conditions in Florida citrus belt - FASS.
newsitem.headline: Spring-like conditions in Florida citrus belt - FASS.

text.p: The citrus belt had scattered showers this week with temperatures in the 80's, the Florida Agricultural Statistics Service (FASS), said. The spring-like conditions have many caretakers fertilizing and irrigating in expectance of new growth. However, any new growth will be vulnerable to frost or freezing weather should any arrive.
According to FASS, picking crews are rapidly winding up their early and midseason orange harvest.
Caretakers are discing and chopping following fertilization.
FASS reported an estimated 105,000 boxes of navel oranges were harvested in the week ended February 16, down from 161,000 boxes the previous week and 267,000 boxes in the week ended February 2.
An estimated 7,155,000 boxes of early and mid oranges were harvested in the week ended February 16, down from 9,124,000 boxes the prior week and 10,192,000 boxes the week ended February 2, FASS said.
